extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent prosecutors, and drafters preparing U.S. patent applications (with awareness of EPO/SEP/EPO added-matter concerns)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical drafting guidance for preparing U.S. patent specifications and claims, with attention to prosecution, litigation, standard-essential patents, fintech inventions, and EPO added-matter issues. Emphasizes defensible specification drafting because the specification is rarely changed after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Principle: specification is rarely changeable
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification can rarely be changed during prosecution, so the applicant only gets one opportunity to explain how the invention works; claims must be read in light of the specification and a carefully drafted specification is therefore particularly important for later claim construction in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft the specification to anticipate future claim construction and litigation; treat the specification as the primary record that will constrain claim interpretation. Avoid relying on the idea that prosecution amendments will fix missing disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use consistent terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the same terms throughout the specification and claims; avoid using interchangeable terms that could be construed as different concepts by examiners or courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: don’t alternate between 'pharmaceutical formulation' and 'pharmaceutical composition' because an examiner (e.g., EPO Examiner) might treat them as distinct and refuse to combine embodiments. Define terms where necessary and stick to those definitions across the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for future claim combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a drafting structure that supports later combining of claim elements and dependencies so you can pursue different claim scopes during prosecution and litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques: file multiply dependent claims and/or include a 'numbered embodiments' section to provide clear basis for later combinations. Draft originally-filed claims that can be re-used as fallback positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft with litigation and invalidation in mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft the specification and claims anticipating enforcement and possible invalidation challenges; avoid language or characterizations that could unintentionally limit claim scope or admit prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make statements that limit scope unnecessarily (e.g., overly definitive descriptions); avoid characterizing the prior art in a way that admits elements as known. Favor wording that preserves alternative claim constructions and avoids narrowing admissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'patent profanity' (limiting language/phrases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain common phrases and words can be read as limiting and shrink claim scope if used carelessly in the specification or claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid or use carefully: 'the invention is' / 'the present invention', 'must' / 'essential' / 'critical' / 'necessary', 'always' / 'every' / 'only', and 'preferred' when it functions to limit rather than merely identify a preferred embodiment. Phrase descriptions to avoid unintended limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a strong written description
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the specification supplies robust written-description support for the full breadth of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include multiple embodiments and examples that cover the breadth of the claimed invention; use pictures, diagrams, and formulas where helpful; provide explicit definitions for ambiguous or novel terms to establish support for claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting for standard-essential patents (SEP) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When drafting patents likely to be asserted as standard-essential, tailor the specification and claims to facilitate mapping to standards and implementations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate how a claim chart will map patent features to the standard; use the standard's terminology where possible; cover both upstream and downstream implementations; capture mandatory features of the standard explicitly so the patent can be mapped to required elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintech-specific drafting strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: For financial-technology inventions, draft to emphasize technical improvements and avoid claims that read as purely financial methods (which risk Alice rejections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie claimed methods to specific computer architectures and document network, security, or efficiency improvements. Avoid claiming pure financial transactions or only financial improvements; show how the invention achieves a technological solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid added matter (EPO particular concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that every claimed feature has explicit original-filed support and avoid intermediate generalizations that could create added-matter issues under EPO practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit basis for each claim feature in the original filing; avoid intermediate generalizations (i.e., extracting and claiming aspects that were only disclosed in combination without basis); consider numbered embodiments to show how features can be combined; be careful with adjectives (e.g., 'low-power' might not support a claim to 'less than 5 watts'). Write claims and disclosure so originally-filed claims can serve as fallback positions.
